entries.1f0768fda71ba222: The securities report says the main ingredients combine sugars and minerals, which are also found in body fluids, in a unique balance, and that the products are non-oil, non-alcohol and uncolored, with elements that cause skin and hair problems removed as far as possible. As the securities report describes it as a “fabless company,” it has no factories; planning and in-house formulation are carried out at the Tokyo Research Institute (Chuo-ku, Tokyo) and the Central Research Institute (Chuo-ku, Kobe), and manufacturing is entrusted to external contract manufacturing plants. entries.35b36caed178b719: For the fiscal year ended March 2026, gross profit was ¥2,563 million (down 3.5% from the previous year) and selling, general and administrative expenses were ¥2,392 million (down 5.4%), so operating profit was ¥170 million (¥126 million in the previous year). The securities report says the decline in gross profit caused by lower revenue was covered by reductions in SG&A expenses, including IT-related costs, advertising expenses, R&D expenses and depreciation. Ordinary profit was ¥200 million (up 48.3% year on year), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥142 million (up 251.1%), including special gains of ¥21 million from the sale of investment securities. There are no borrowings, and cash and cash equivalents total ¥2,134 million. The securities report says it expects consolidated operating profit for the next fiscal year to be ¥50 million (down 70.2% from the current year), reflecting a plan for SG&A expenses to increase, including promotion costs for new products, personnel costs and IT-related costs.

entries.4c98fe2119b04bb8: The company, a pure holding company, and three [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]] make up a group that plans and develops cosmetics for salons and sells them through agents or directly to salons. The business is a [[term:segment|single segment]] covering the product planning, research and development, and sale of cosmetics, together with the related service operations. The basic model is for salons to counsel consumers and sell products to them, and the products handled fall into three categories: skincare, haircare and other. It has no factories and outsources manufacturing to external contract manufacturing plants. The securities report says it has worked to provide high-quality, safe and reliable cosmetics and to support salon management.

entries.965c49e1e17fe88d: This is the Group's business of handling cosmetics for hair and beauty salons, esthetic salons, nail salons, eyelash salons, beauty clinics and similar establishments (which the securities report calls "salons"), from product planning through research and development to sales.
entries.982dfe5f40087cb6: This is the Group's business of planning, developing, researching and selling cosmetics for hair salons, beauty salons, nail salons, eyelash salons, beauty clinics and others (the securities report calls these 'salons'), from product planning through research and development to sales. The securities report states that because this is the only segment in the business, it does not present segment-by-segment information. The products are described as containing sugars and minerals also found in body fluids, in a proprietary balance, with factors that cause skin and hair problems removed as far as possible. Sales take the form in which the consolidated subsidiary Adjuvant Cosme Japan Co., Ltd. sells products to salons, either through agents or directly, and the salons sell to consumers through counseling. The company also holds seminars and hands-on sessions for salons to convey product explanations and sales knowledge and skills. 2C Co., Ltd. delivers hair-growth products directly to consumers through EC, and ADJUVANT GLOBAL COMPANY LIMITED in Hong Kong sells products directly to salons and also carries out promotions aimed at general consumers. Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,813 million (down 6.9% year on year), with domestic revenue of ¥3,654 million (95.8% of the total) and overseas revenue of ¥158 million (4.2% of the total). The number of salons with which the company did business during the period (the 'number of active salons' in the securities report) was 14,609, an increase of 1,943 from the same period last year. Products are handled in the following three categories, and revenue for each category is stated before deducting sales rebates not allocated to the categories. In addition, the securities report notes that 2C Co., Ltd. merged with Adjuvant Cosme Japan Co., Ltd. effective March 21, 2026. The company transitioned to a pure holding company structure effective September 21, 2021.
entries.a0808fb17dedd207: This category covers shampoo, treatment, scalp cleansing, scalp lotion, styling products, hair color and other products. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,668 million (down 2.6% year on year), the largest of the three categories, at a 70.0% share. The securities report explains that although sales of products such as the outbath styling product 'muts totte (Myūtsu Totte)' were strong owing to strengthened sales support centered on products launched in June 2025, this was not enough to offset declines in sales of existing products, and revenue decreased year on year.

entries.ac587c00ca7f83ca: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥3,813 million, down 6.9% from the previous year. Revenue by product category was haircare ¥2,668 million (down 2.6% year on year), skincare ¥1,353 million (down 11.2%) and other ¥84 million (down 54.7%). These three category amounts are before deducting sales rebates; consolidated revenue is the total after deducting sales rebates. The securities report says haircare benefited from stronger sales support centered on products launched in June 2025, with “muts totte” performing well, and that in skincare some brands grew through special campaigns aimed at new loyal customers, but neither was enough to offset declines in sales of existing products. Revenue is, in principle, recognized at the point when products are delivered.
